desc:
A marketing review and approval process makes sure a person checks every claim before content goes live. Ecom Swift LLC maps who writes, reviews and approves, builds the checklist and sets it up in tools you already use.

## What is a marketing review and approval process?

A marketing review and approval process is a short set of steps that every piece of content passes before publication. A writer finishes a draft, a reviewer checks it against a list and an approver says yes or sends it back. The process works for ads, emails, product pages, blog posts and social posts.

It does not need special software. A shared sheet, a board or a folder with clear statuses is enough when the rules are clear.

## Why fast content needs a safety check

Modern tools let a team produce text and images in minutes. That speed is useful, but it also makes mistakes travel quickly. A wrong price, a made-up feature, a health claim or a photo you have no right to use can reach customers before anyone notices.

The costs of these errors are real: refunds, rejected ads, complaints, account warnings and lost trust. A review step catches most of them early, when fixing a line takes seconds. It also protects your reputation, because customers learn to rely on what you publish. The process cannot prevent every error or decide legal questions, but it lowers the chance that an avoidable one goes out.

## What a good review system includes

- A checklist for claims: prices, dates, features, comparisons and promises.
- A separate list for sensitive areas such as health, money and safety.
- Image checks for rights, credit and whether a picture shows the real product.
- Platform rules for each channel where you publish.
- Named roles for writer, reviewer and approver, so no step is skipped.
- A status board that shows what is drafted, in review, approved and live.
- A log of claims with their sources, so a statement can be traced later.
- Rules for text that was drafted with the help of writing tools.
- A clear route for risky content, with someone who decides what to do.
- A short guide that new team members can follow on their first day.

## How we set it up

We begin by learning how content moves through your business today: who writes it, who sees it and where it gets stuck. Then we design the smallest set of steps that would have caught your past mistakes and build the checklist around your real products and channels.

We create the board or sheet in a tool you already use and test the process on three of your actual pieces, so you can see it find problems. The Basic package gives you a checklist, roles and a simple flow on one page. Standard adds the status board, a claim and source log, checklists for each content type and the live test. Premium adds image rights tracking, rules for tool-assisted text, an escalation route, team training and a short period of light support afterward.

This is a workflow service, not legal advice. For legal questions, speak to a qualified professional.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the checklist short enough that people use it.
- Make the reviewer someone other than the writer.
- Record where each important fact came from.
- Allow the reviewer to say no without a debate.
- Update the checklist after every mistake.

**Avoid:**
- Approving content because a deadline is close.
- Letting one person write, review and approve alone.
- Adding so many steps that people avoid the process.
- Reusing an image without confirming its source.
- Treating a tool's draft as already verified.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small team that publishes on several channels and has no formal checking. It suits a store that sells items with strict rules around claims, such as supplements or skincare, and needs extra care. It also suits an owner who has had one embarrassing mistake and wants to prevent a second.

## What we need from you

Tell us who creates and approves content, which tools you use and where you publish. Share two or three past mistakes, if there are any, and pieces we can use for the test. If we set up a board in your tool, we ask for a team or collaborator role, never a password.
